paragraphs: AeroCloud Systems sells cloud-based airport management software that airport teams use to run daily operations. Three lines make up the offer: an airport operations system, passenger processing, and passenger flow monitoring under the name AeroCloud Optic.

The operations system is modular, so an airport pays for the pieces it needs and adds more later. The common use and self-service tools are aimed at airports, airlines, fixed base operators and ground handlers moving passengers from arrival to boarding. AeroCloud Optic counts and tracks passengers as they move, so teams can find bottlenecks and predict queue times. The company states there are no user limits and no licence fees, with role-based permissions deciding who sees what.

Customer stories on the site include one about Palm Springs International Airport. Another covers Frankfurt Airport. AeroCloud says it has teams across the US and Europe. Support is offered around the clock by staff the company describes as knowing the realities of airport operations.
